''48. Not in hou{{ls}}es.''] The vulgar Heretikes alleage this place again{{ls}}t the corporal being of Chri{{ls}}t in the B. Sacrament & in Churches: by which rea{{ls}}on they might haue driuen him out of al hou{{ls}}es, Churches, and corporal places, when he vvas vi{{ls}}ible in earth. But it is meant of the Diuinitie only, & {{ls}}poken to correct the carnal Ievves: {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=God is not conteined in place, yet he vvil be vvor{{ls}}hipped in one place more then in an other.}}Who thought God either {{ls}}o to be conteined, compa{{ls}}{{ls}}ed, and limited to their Temple, that he could be no vvhere els, or at lea{{ls}}t that he vvould not heare or receiue mens praiers and {{ls}}acrifices in the Churches of the Gentiles, or els vvhere, out of the {{ls}}aid Temple. And {{ls}}o as it maketh nothing for the Sacramentaries, no more doth it {{ls}}erue for {{ls}}uch as e{{ls}}teeme Churches and places of publike praier no more conuenient nor more holy then any other profane hou{{ls}}es or chambers. For though his per{{ls}}on or vertue be not limited to any place, yet it plea{{ls}}eth him conde{{ls}}cending to our nece{{ls}}{{ls}}itie and profite, to vvorke his vvonders and to be vvor{{ls}}hipped of vs in holy places rather then profane.
